newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil slips, IPE expiry brakes trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil slips, IPE expiry brakes trade.

text.p: NWE physical gas oil trade slowed to a crawl on Tuesday as traders sought to protect themselves from potential volatility caused by a record high physical delivery against the November IPE contract.
An unusually large 865,100 tonnes was delivered into the contract in the second half of November to settle open positions, putting pressure on values.
IPE November futures expired 50 cents down at $220 a tonne and the December contract slipped $1 to $211, with higher European stocks adding to downward pressure.
A trading house said by other players to have a dominant long position in November IPE futures said without elaborating it had fixed two vessels to move arbitrage product to Asia.

Traders at other companies said this involved much of the material delivered into the contract. "We think they know what they are doing and they have demand for it," one said. "They locked in an arb to India long before. I really don't think they are going to come on the (European) market that much at all."
A barge of refinery grade prompt heating oil sold at Dec IPE +$8.25.
